# PKCS#7 interop fixture

Test-only material.  Nothing here is secret: the private keys are generated by
`gen.sh` in a temporary directory and never committed.

## Why

The PKCS#7 signer/verifier (`sign.go` plus the forked
`github.com/varwof/pkcs7`) is our own code, so a test where we sign and then
verify only proves internal consistency.  **openssl is the independent
oracle**: it is the reference implementation of CMS/RFC 5652, and R1 was exactly
a case where the fork agreed with itself but not with the standard (it located
the signer by serial number alone).

## What is covered

`pkcs7_interop_test.go` pins both directions:

| test | direction | needs openssl |
|---|---|---|
| `TestPKCS7InteropFixtureOpenSSLSignature` | committed openssl signature → Go verifier accepts (and rejects a tampered content) | no |
| `TestPKCS7InteropOpenSSLSignsGoVerifies` | live openssl sign → Go verifier accepts | yes |
| `TestPKCS7InteropGoSignsOpenSSLVerifies` | `SignCapability` → `openssl cms -verify` accepts | yes |

The live tests skip when `openssl` is absent (Windows runner) or is LibreSSL
(the default `/usr/bin/openssl` on macOS runners, which lacks `req -addext`);
the committed-fixture test still runs everywhere, so the interop contract keeps
being regression-checked even where the live cross-check cannot run.

## Files

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `content.json` | the signed content |
| `root.pem` | self-signed test root CA (EC P-256) |
| `signer.pem` | signer leaf, `extendedKeyUsage=codeSigning` (the usage the verifier requires) |
| `openssl.p7s` | detached PKCS#7/CMS over `content.json`, produced by `openssl cms -sign` |
| `gen.sh` | regenerates the three files above (generates keys in a temp dir) |

## Regenerating

```bash
testdata/pkcs7-interop/gen.sh
```

Requires OpenSSL 3.  The committed certificates are valid for 100 years, so the
fixture does not silently expire.
